ownership_reason: Only the gold writes the entries of the vector: it increases the entries the vector holds and then sets each remaining zero entry to the value. Hops 1-3 pass the vector and the value along; hop 4 only marks the held entries (its sparse iterator). Without the membership test, the gold's second pass also writes the value over a held entry that its own first pass has just made zero, whatever mask it is given, so no caller can pre-filter or restore it (the old value is gone). The gold's javadoc promises that the value is added to the entries; on the trigger 2 - 2 is written as -2. The convention is pinned outside the gold: SparseFieldVector.mapAddToSelf and ArrayRealVector.mapAddToSelf add the value to every entry, a zero sum included, and the two-pass sparse sibling OpenMapRealVector.getDistance(OpenMapRealVector) picks the remaining entries of its second pass by membership (containsKey), not by value; ArrayRealVectorTest::testMapFunctions and SparseFieldVectorTest::testMapFunctions (the same {1, 2, 3} - 2 = {-1, 0, 1}), SparseRealVectorTest::testPredicates and SparseRealVectorTest::testBasicFunctions pass.
